source_evidence: the issuer promises to pay you a specified rate of interest during the life of the bond and to repay the principal, also known as face value or par value of the bond, when it "matures," or comes due after a set period of time.
question: What are interest, principal, and maturity in a bond?
answer: Interest is the payment the issuer promises to make during the bond’s life. Principal, also called face value or par value, is the amount the issuer promises to repay when the bond matures. Maturity is the set time when the bond comes due.
